messages:
alex: rolled out canary for adaptive-microburst-smoothing in us-west-2 at 07:45 PT. idea: smooth microbatch windows for tiny bursts so short high-concurrency flows don't create tail spikes.

maya: top-line numbers?

alex: 07:45-08:05 (5% traffic): requests 9.4k; p50 20ms -> 12ms (-40%); p95 270ms -> 160ms (-41%); p99 720ms -> 480ms (-33%). est token-cost -12%. error-rate stable.

kai: any regressions on rerankers or streaming clients?

alex: rerankers unaffected (they batch larger); streaming first-token unchanged. saw a narrow case where very bursty SDK clients saw +3ms p50 due to smoothing; added client-id override to skip smoothing for flagged SDKs.

deploy-bot: rollout: smoothing-controller v1.0.0 -> canary(5%) (deploy id: d-20260325-04)

sree: what's the ramp and rollback plan?

alex: ramp 5% -> 30% in 8h if p95 <= 1.5x baseline -> 80% in 36h -> 100% in 48h. auto-rollback: errors > baseline*2 for 5m OR p99 > baseline*1.7 for 3m. manual rollback if dogfood flags user-visible quality issues.

lina: Dedicated/billing impact?

alex: no change to Dedicated placement or billing; this only alters scheduling inside shared runtime. we'll add a Route Analytics tile with adoption and projected savings and a short note for Product.

maya: action items: 1) add console tile (alex) 2) run extended evals on bursty SDK traces (kai) 3) monitor canary + synthetic burst tests (sree). :rocket:
